第 27 章 The First Two Questions to Ask When Your Team Is Struggling团队挣扎时要问的前两个问题

Cate Huston / 凯特·休斯顿

— 第 81 页 —

I've never stepped into a leadership role without it quickly becoming clear why a new leader was needed. I think it's normal for companies to hire new leaders when there are problems that need to be addressed. So, I suspect that as the congratulations die down, it's also normal to look at the set of problems that surround you and ask, "Where do I begin?" (also normal: "What have I done?!"). I suggest, instead, starting with these two questions:

我每次走上领导岗位，都很快清楚为什么需要新领导。我认为公司在有问题需要解决时招聘新领导是正常的。所以，我猜当祝贺声平息后，看着周围一堆问题问「我从哪里开始？」也是正常的（同样正常的是：「我做了什么？！」）。我的建议是，从这两个问题开始：

  • How do I create clarity?我如何创造清晰性？
  • How do I create capacity?我如何创造产能？

How Do I Create Clarity?我如何创造清晰性？

Every struggling team I have encountered seems to be experiencing some kind of existential crisis about "who we are" or "what is our purpose." Often this crisis is framed as a need for defining a "vision," but as a pragmatist (and someone who frankly hates the word "vision"), this seems beside the point. If we're not shipping, how much does it matter what we're not shipping? How can we possibly know what we should be doing two or five years from now if we don't have a consistent idea of what we are doing today?

我遇到的每个挣扎中的团队似乎都在经历某种关于「我们是谁」或「我们的目的是什么」的存在主义危机。通常这个危机被框定为需要定义「愿景」，但作为一个实用主义者（而且坦白说讨厌「愿景」这个词），这好像偏题了。如果我们不交付，我们不交付什么又有多大关系？如果我们对今天在做什么都没有一致的认识，我们怎么可能知道两三年或五年后应该做什么？

Here's the thing about the "vision" problem: it's a comfortable one. No one on the team feels threatened by it, because it's largely someone else's problem. Everyone can have an opinion about it, because it's abstract enough that most people won't have to do anything to shape or change it. Vision debates are the "bikeshedding" of team purpose and structure: They're the sideshow discussions people have in order to avoid confronting more pertinent problems.

关于「愿景」问题是这样的：它是一个让人舒服的问题。团队里没人觉得受威胁，因为它很大程度上是别人的问题。每个人都可以有意见，因为它足够抽象，大多数人不需要做任何事来塑造或改变它。愿景辩论是团队目的和结构的「自行车棚效应」：它们是人们为了避免面对更切题的问题而进行的杂耍讨论。

— 第 82 页 —

Clarity is more difficult because it's more immediate and must be based on what's happening today—which means you need to confront what's actually happening today—there's no hiding behind "lack of vision." Are teams delivering? Are projects drifting on and on with no end in sight? Are we doing things because they are interesting or because they are valuable?

清晰性更难，因为它更即时、必须基于今天正在发生什么——这意味着你需要面对今天实际在发生什么——不能躲在「缺乏愿景」后面。团队在交付吗？项目在无尽地漂移、看不到尽头吗？我们做事情是因为它们有趣还是因为它们有价值？

The more concrete we get, the more difficult it is to get everyone in agreement: A wide range of opinions can find shelter in a broad, fuzzy statement in a way that is not possible in a narrow and clear one. Clarity involves hard conversations, hard truths, and defining one, then two, and then three steps ahead. It is challenging work that looks small from the outside—a "no" here, a "no" there, a refinement of this and that. It's often stating what at least some people believed to be true, anyway, such as what isn't going well or what the next steps include.

我们越具体，就越难让所有人达成一致：广泛的意见可以在宽泛模糊的声明中找到庇护所，而在狭窄清晰的声明中则不可能。清晰性需要艰难的对话、艰难的真相，以及定义一步、然后两步、然后三步。这是从外面看起来很小的有挑战性的工作——这里一个「不」，那里一个「不」，这里那里的完善。它往往只是在陈述至少一些人已经认为是真的事情，比如什么不顺利或下一步包括什么。

And yet, it's the most effective way I've found to stop teams from drifting and get them to begin executing.

然而，这是我发现的阻止团队漂移、让他们开始执行的最有效方式。

What actions you can take in order to achieve clarity depend on the team, but typically you might try these:

为了达到清晰性你可以采取什么行动取决于团队，但通常你可以试试这些：

  • Take stock of all ongoing projects as well as the purpose and timeline for each of those projects.盘点所有正在进行的项目以及每个项目的目的和时间线。
  • Clearly define the scope of upcoming milestones in every current (and new) project.清楚定义每个当前（和新）项目中即将到来的里程碑的范围。
  • Articulate the current priorities of the team, the purposes of those priorities, and the rationale behind making them priorities.阐明团队当前的优先级、这些优先级的目的，以及把它们设为优先级背后的理由。
  • Determine timeframes that you can predict (e.g., we are focused on X through the end of Q4) and highlight parallel work that will determine what comes next.确定你可以预测的时间范围（例如，我们专注于 X 直到 Q4 末），并强调决定接下来做什么的并行工作。
  • Make sure project status is visible and that teams have visibility into each other's work (e.g., standup meetings).确保项目状态可见，团队能看到彼此的工作（例如站会）。

How Do I Create Capacity?我如何创造产能？

Struggling teams also commonly suffer from a sense of overload. Often this is very unevenly distributed across the team—some people are exceptionally relaxed, whereas others seem alarmingly overwhelmed.

挣扎中的团队通常也有过载感。通常这种过载在团队中分布非常不均——有些人特别放松，而另一些人似乎令人担忧地不堪重负。

— 第 83 页 —

If you view your team as a system, you'll see where you have bottlenecks that, if cleared, would increase the overall capacity of the team.

如果你把团队看作一个系统，你会看到瓶颈在哪里——如果清除它们，就能增加团队的整体产能。

Perhaps you have teams that are working on too many disparate things (this usually involves people working alone). How do you streamline, focus, and make progress?

也许你的团队在做太多分散的事情（这通常涉及人们单独工作）。你如何精简、聚焦、取得进展？

Perhaps your incoming requests are out of control. How do you stop checking off requests one by one and take a more strategic approach instead? What kind of help do you need to do that?

也许你的进来的请求失控了。你如何停止一个一个地打勾，转而采取更战略性的方式？你需要什么样的帮助？

Perhaps you need to realign people closer to the work that they want to do. Perhaps you need to give some people clear feedback about where they're falling short, and if that doesn't work, start the process of letting them go.

也许你需要把人重新调整到他们想做的工作附近。也许你需要给一些人明确的反馈，告诉他们哪里不足，如果不行，就开始请他们走的流程。

Usually people outside the team (leadership, marketing, etc.) are talking about dates and delivery, but you need to get the team itself estimating its timelines and embracing Continuous Delivery.

通常团队外部的人（领导层、市场部等）在谈论日期和交付，但你需要让团队自己估算时间线并拥抱持续交付。

If you manage managers, improving them as leaders will always create capacity on your team: Their teams will become better, and you can rely on them more and delegate more effectively. Sometimes, it feels like we don't have time to coach the people around us, but medium term—not even long term—we don't have time not to.

如果你管的是经理，把他们提升为领导者总会在你的团队中创造产能：他们的团队会变得更好，你可以更依赖他们、更有效地授权。有时候我们觉得没有时间辅导周围的人，但中期——甚至不用长期——我们没有时间不辅导。

OK, Now What?好了，那现在怎么办？

It's likely that asking these questions has given you a whole lot of work to do. As you are human and can do only so much at once, now comes the question, "What do I do first?"

问了这些问题之后，你可能有一大堆工作要做。作为人，你一次只能做这么多，现在问题来了：「我先做什么？」

Answering this question is a balance between impact and time. The highest impact things you can do will likely take longer, but there are usually several relatively impactful things that won't take too much time. If you're new, you'll also have to balance building trust and demonstrating impact. For example, clearly communicating big-picture information about what is going on to the team is a worthwhile exercise that often uncovers new information is usually relatively quick, and it creates shared understanding across the team of where projects are at.

回答这个问题是在影响力和时间之间平衡。你能做的最高影响力的事情可能需要更长时间，但通常有几个相对有影响力的事情不需要太多时间。如果你是新来的，你还需要在建立信任和展示影响力之间平衡。例如，向团队清楚传达正在发生什么的大局信息是一个有价值的练习，通常相对快速，而且能在团队中创造对项目状态的共同理解。

However, these smaller time investments will not have any impact unless we also take on some bigger ones. For example, there is nothing more corrosive to overall output than when one or more teams has a lead who is struggling or just isn't a good fit. Addressing this kind of situation is never straightforward and never easy—the only thing worse and more difficult, ultimately, is letting it continue unaddressed.

然而，这些小的时间投资不会有任何影响，除非我们也承担一些更大的。例如，对整体产出最有腐蚀性的莫过于一个或多个团队的负责人在挣扎或就是不合适。处理这种情况从来不简单、不容易——最终唯一更糟更难的是让它继续不被处理。

— 第 84 页 —

Every situation is different, so my suggestion is to write down a list of ideas for each, talk them over with your boss, a trusted peer, or a coach, and then begin taking them on one or two at a time. Just remember the list isn't static: as teams evolve, the bottlenecks change, and you'll need to keep asking these questions, revisiting and adjusting as you go.

每种情况都不同，所以我的建议是为每个问题写下想法清单，和你的老板、可信任的同事或教练讨论，然后一次开始做一两个。记住清单不是静态的：随着团队演进，瓶颈会变，你需要不断问这些问题，一边走一边回顾和调整。
